# How to translate this chunk

This file holds `items`, a list of `{"k", "ctx", "t"}`. `t` is English text
that a reader of an Indian app or website sees. `ctx` is the field it came
from, such as label, hint, button, documents, brief or title. Use it to judge
tone and length: a label stays short, a hint can be a sentence.

Write `{"items": [{"k": ..., "t": ...}, ...]}` to the path in `write_to`.
Keep every `k` unchanged and in the same order. Put the translation in `t`.
Leave out `ctx`. Do not add, merge, split or drop items.

## Keep these exactly as they are

- Placeholders and markup: `{0}`, `{name}`, `%s`, `%d`, `%1$s`, HTML tags, `\n`.
- Website addresses, e-mail addresses and links.
- Every number: phone and toll-free numbers, Aadhaar, account, IFSC, PAN, PIN
  codes, amounts, dates, percentages. Write digits as 0-9, the Western digits,
  in every language, including Urdu. People type these into forms that take
  Western digits.
- Acronyms people know in Latin letters: OTP, PAN, IFSC, UPI, KYC, e-KYC, DBT,
  BPL, APL, NFSA, PM-KISAN, SMS, PDF, ID.

## Names

- Product, app, portal and scheme names: transliterate them into the script so
  they read naturally. Keep any acronym inside them in Latin, so "APPSC
  portal" becomes APPSC followed by the word for portal.
- A button or menu label quoted from a website, such as 'Apply Online' or
  'Register', stays in English inside quotes. The reader has to find that exact
  English word on the screen.
- People and places in examples are transliterated, never replaced with other
  names.
- Government office titles are transliterated so the reader can say them at
  the counter: Tahsildar, Patwari, Talathi, Mamlatdar, BDO, Collector, Gram
  Panchayat. The language notes below give the usual local forms.

## Tone

Write for an ordinary person who may be elderly and may have had little
schooling. Use everyday spoken language, not heavy official vocabulary. Where
people really say the English word, write it in the script: online, form,
portal, login, mobile, bank, certificate, download, upload, app. Keep
instructions short and direct, in the form "do this".

"Gender" means sex (male or female). It is never the word for caste.

## Before you write

Check that you have the same number of items as the input and that every
number and placeholder came through. Write the whole file in ONE Write call,
as valid UTF-8 JSON with no `\u` escapes and nothing else in the file.

items.t: Money to build a pucca house for a village family that has no house or lives in a kutcha one: Rs.1.20 lakh in the plains and Rs.1.30 lakh in hill states, the North-East and difficult areas, paid into the bank account in instalments as the house goes up. On top of that the family gets 90 days of paid labour (95 in hilly areas) on its own house under the rural job scheme, and Rs.12,000 for a toilet. Families are picked from the SECC 2011 list and the new Awaas+ 2024 survey and checked by the Gram Sabha; homeless and destitute families, manual scavengers, primitive tribal groups and freed bonded labourers come first. The scheme runs till March 2029 for 2 crore more houses.
Rs.1.20 lakh (Rs.1.30 lakh in hill and NE areas), plus 90–95 days' wages and Rs.12,000 for a toilet
Village family with no house, or living in a kutcha house (kutcha walls and roof, up to 2 rooms)
Name on the SECC 2011 Permanent Wait List, or found eligible in the Awaas+ 2024 survey and passed by the Gram Sabha
Ruled out if any member owns a pucca house, a motorised 3- or 4-wheeler or mechanised farm machinery, or has a KCC limit of Rs.50,000 or more
Ruled out if any member is a government employee, earns over Rs.15,000 a month, pays income or professional tax, or runs a government-registered business
Ruled out if the family owns 2.5 acres or more of irrigated land with irrigation equipment, or 5 acres or more of unirrigated land
Owning a two-wheeler, fridge, landline or motorised fishing boat no longer rules a family out (changed in 2024)
Aadhaar card of the head of family and members (face e-KYC is done during the survey)
Bank or post office account seeded with Aadhaar
Job card under the rural employment scheme
Swachh Bharat Mission (SBM) number, if the family already has one
Paper for the plot where the house will be built (patta or possession proof); landless families are given land by the state

Gram Panchayat office: tell the Panchayat Secretary or the Gram Rozgar Sahayak that you want to be surveyed under Awaas+ 2024, and take your Aadhaar, job card, bank passbook and mobile phone. The Block Development Office (BDO) registers the approved names; complaints go to the BDO or the District Rural Development Agency.
Aadhaar number of head of household
Checked by a face scan through the AadhaarFaceRD app; no fingerprint or OTP is needed.
Name of head of household
Shanti Devi
Exactly as on Aadhaar. A woman head of family is welcome; the house is usually sanctioned in the woman's name or jointly.
Family members
4 (Shanti Devi, Ramu, Geeta, Sonu)
Add every member living and cooking together, each with Aadhaar.
Social category
SC, ST, minority or other. This decides which priority list your family goes into.
Type of present house
Kutcha walls and kutcha roof, 1 room
Describe the house as it is today. More than 2 rooms with a pucca roof makes the family ineligible.
Monthly income of highest earner
The member who earns the most. Above Rs.15,000 a month rules the family out.
Land owned
0.5 acre unirrigated
Write irrigated and unirrigated land separately, as in the land record.
Photo of present house
Geo-tagged photo taken in the app
Taken standing at the house, so the location is recorded with the photo.
Job card number
From your rural employment job card. The 90 days of paid work on your house are booked against it.
An account in the beneficiary's own name, seeded with Aadhaar. All instalments come here.
Ask at the Gram Panchayat whether your name is already on the Permanent Wait List, or look up the Panchayat-wise list on the PMAY-G website.
If it is not, get surveyed under Awaas+ 2024: the Panchayat surveyor fills the form on the AwaasPlus app, or you survey yourself on the app with a face scan where your state's survey is open.
The Gram Sabha reads out and checks the list, objections are heard at the block and district, and approved families are ranked by priority.
When your turn comes, the Block office registers you on AwaasSoft, geo-tags your old house and plot, and issues the sanction order. The first instalment comes into your Aadhaar-seeded account.
Build the house, at least 25 sq m with a kitchen. At each stage (plinth, lintel, roof) the official takes a geo-tagged photo and the next instalment is released.
Work on your own house under the rural job scheme for 90 (or 95) days' wages, and claim Rs.12,000 for the toilet through the Panchayat.
Finish within 12 months. Track payments with Search Beneficiary or FTO Tracking on the PMAY-G site, and go to the BDO if an instalment is stuck.
1800-11-6446 (PMAY-G helpline) / support-pmayg@gov.in; Block Development Office for local complaints
Pradhan Mantri Divyangjan Pension Yojana (formerly IGNDPS)
Ministry of Rural Development — Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly NSAP)

A monthly pension for persons with severe disability who belong to a below-poverty-line household. It was called the Indira Gandhi National Disability Pension Scheme (IGNDPS) until the Union Cabinet renamed it on 14 October 2026, as part of the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly NSAP). The Cabinet also approved Rs.375 a month (Rs.625 from age 80), a 40 per cent disability limit instead of 80, and no minimum age; these start once the new guidelines are issued, due by mid-January 2027. Until then the old rules apply — age 18 or more and a certificate showing 80 per cent or more — and the state adds its own top-up.
Rs.300/month (Rs.500 after age 80) from the Centre, plus the state top-up; rising to Rs.375 (Rs.625 after age 80) once the new guidelines are issued
Age 18 years or more on the date of application (no minimum age once the new guidelines are issued)
Severe or multiple disability of 80 per cent or more, certified by the competent medical authority (40 per cent or more once the new guidelines are issued)
Disability certificate showing 80 per cent or more (40 per cent once the new guidelines are issued), issued by the Chief Medical Officer or a district medical board
Under the current rules you must be 18 or above. Once the new guidelines are issued, there is no minimum age.
Under the current rules it must read 80 per cent or more, or the Block office refuses it. Once the new guidelines are issued (due by mid-January 2027), 40 per cent or more qualifies.

Get the disability certificate in hand before anything else. The Chief Medical Officer's board at the district hospital assesses free of charge on fixed weekly days — ask the hospital's disability desk for the day. The certificate must show 80 per cent or more under the current rules, and 40 per cent or more once the new guidelines are issued.
Pradhan Mantri Kisan Maandhan Yojana (PM-KMY, farmer pension)
Ministry of Agriculture & Farmers Welfare (run with LIC and CSC)

A pension of Rs.3,000 a month from age 60 for small and marginal farmers who join between 18 and 40. You pay Rs.55 to Rs.200 a month, depending on your age when you join, and the government adds the same amount. The monthly amount can be cut automatically from your PM-Kisan money. You join at a Common Service Centre (CSC) with your Aadhaar and bank passbook.
Rs.3,000 a month pension from age 60; Rs.1,500 family pension to the spouse
Small and marginal farmers with up to 2 hectares (about 5 acres) of cultivable land in their own name in the land records
Age 18 to 40 years when joining; you pay every month until you turn 60
Not for people already in NPS, ESIC or EPFO, or who joined PM Shram Yogi Maandhan or PM Vyapari Maandhan
Not for income-tax payers, government or PSU employees (Class IV / Group D staff can join), doctors, engineers, lawyers, CAs and architects in practice, or holders of constitutional posts
You need an Aadhaar card and a savings bank account
Savings bank passbook or cheque with IFSC (the PM-Kisan account if you want the amount cut from PM-Kisan)

Name and date of birth of your spouse and of the nominee

Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana (National Family Benefit Scheme, NFBS)
Ministry of Rural Development — National Social Assistance Programme (Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana)

A one-time payment of Rs.20,000 to a poor (BPL) family when its main earning member dies between the ages of 18 and 59, from illness, accident or any other cause. A woman who runs the home counts as a breadwinner too. The money goes to the family member who, after a local inquiry, becomes the new head of the household. This is the old National Family Benefit Scheme (NFBS), renamed Pradhan Mantri Parivar Labh Yojana by the Cabinet on 14 October 2026 with the benefit unchanged, so local offices may still use the old name.
Rs.20,000 one-time payment to the family, into the bank account
The family is below the poverty line (BPL) on the state's list. An eligible poor family missing from the list should still be considered
The person who died was the main earner of the household. A woman who looked after the home also counts
The death happened when that person was more than 18 and less than 60 years old
Any cause of death counts: illness, accident or anything else
Paid once for each such death, to the surviving member found to be the new head of the household (spouse, minor children, unmarried daughters and dependent parents make up the household)
Death certificate of the breadwinner from the Registrar of Births and Deaths
Age proof of the person who died (birth or school certificate, Aadhaar or voter ID) showing an age between 18 and 59
BPL ration card, or the family's BPL list number
First page of the bank or post-office passbook in the applicant's own name
FIR and post-mortem report, if the death was an accident
Residence proof and two passport-size photographs
Income certificate or legal heir / family certificate, where the state asks for it

The office your state has named for this scheme: usually the Tehsil or SDM office, the Block Development Office, or the District / Tehsil Social Welfare Officer. In a village the Gram Panchayat secretary can take it and forward it; in a town, the municipal office. Most offices give their own form free; the government's model form is Annexe III (page 47) of the NSAP guidelines PDF. Take the filled form with the death certificate, the age proof of the person who died, the BPL ration card, your Aadhaar, your passbook and two photos, plus the FIR and post-mortem report for an accidental death. Some states also take this application online through their e-District or social welfare portal, or at a CSC.

A verification officer checks the facts, normally within two weeks. The case is then placed before the Gram Sabha or ward sabha and sent to the sanctioning officer (BDO, Tehsildar / SDM or District Social Welfare Officer).
The guidelines say the decision should come within 60 days of applying. You get a sanction order and Rs.20,000 is sent to your bank account.
If it is rejected, the reason must be given to you in writing. Appeal to the appellate officer your state names, usually the SDM or a district officer.

Pradhan Mantri Vidhawa Pension Yojana (formerly IGNWPS)

A monthly pension for widows aged 40 and above in below-poverty-line households. It was called the Indira Gandhi National Widow Pension Scheme (IGNWPS) until the Union Cabinet renamed it on 14 October 2026, as part of the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly NSAP); the amount and rules stay the same. The Centre pays a fixed share and the state adds its own top-up. The pension stops if the widow remarries, and converts to the old-age pension once she turns 60 in states that run both.
Pradhan Mantri Vridhavastha Pension Yojana (formerly IGNOAPS)

A monthly pension for people aged 60 and above who belong to a below-poverty-line household. It was called the Indira Gandhi National Old Age Pension Scheme (IGNOAPS) until the Union Cabinet renamed it on 14 October 2026, as part of the Pradhan Mantri Samajik Sahayata Yojana (formerly the National Social Assistance Programme, NSAP); the amount and rules stay the same. The Centre pays a fixed share and almost every state adds a top-up, so the amount that actually reaches the bank account is usually larger than the central figure.
DAY-NRLM Self-Help Group (Aajeevika SHG / Lakhpati Didi)
Ministry of Rural Development — Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana-National Rural Livelihoods Mission, through each State Rural Livelihoods Mission

Women from poor village families join a self-help group (SHG) of 10 to 20 women who save a small sum every week and lend to each other. A group that runs well gets a Revolving Fund of Rs.20,000–30,000, can borrow up to Rs.2.5 lakh from the Community Investment Fund through its village federation, and gets bank loans without collateral at a low rate. Members are trained and supported to take up dairy, farming or small businesses, with the aim of earning Rs.1 lakh a year as a 'Lakhpati Didi'. About 10 crore women are in these groups; you join through your village organisation or the block office of your state's livelihood mission, such as JEEViKA in Bihar, UMED in Maharashtra or Kudumbashree in Kerala.
Revolving Fund Rs.20,000–30,000 per group, up to Rs.2.5 lakh CIF per group, bank loans at 7% up to Rs.3 lakh
